description: Run the two P2 exploratory configs on the live B300 box, strictly timeboxed: c4-tp8-eagle-triton (tp=8 + EAGLE with the triton MoE runner instead of megamoe, to compare MoE backends on Blackwell) and c5-4x-tp2-router (four INDEPENDENT tp=2 engine processes plus a router, reproducing the real awslabs dsv4flash-b300-intra-3p1d topology). Both are allowed to fail: a clean, well-documented failure with the exact error is a legitimate result here and is far cheaper than an open-ended debugging session at $50/hr. Independent of each other; c4 first because it is the cheaper experiment.
steps: Add config c4-tp8-eagle-triton: identical to c1-tp8-eagle-megamoe but replace --moe-a2a-backend megamoe with --moe-runner-backend triton, keep everything else including EAGLE 3/1/4 and the jitcache mount. Be aware this may hit the same 'AssertionError: Hidden size mismatch' in fused_moe_triton/.../fused_moe.py that killed all four B200 attempts during CUDA graph capture; if it does, that is the answer to the megamoe-vs-triton question on Blackwell. Capture the assertion text and traceback file path into matrix-status.json failure_reason and stop - do not attempt padding workarounds.
Run c4 with a reduced readiness timeout (--timeout-sec 1500 is enough now that the JIT cache is warm) so a hang cannot silently burn 40 minutes.

Add config c5-4x-tp2-router. This must use FOUR INDEPENDENT engine processes each at tp=2, not one process with --dp 4: one unified process with --enable-dp-attention --dp N is already proven to die with 'AssertionError: short-circuiting allreduce will lead to hangs', and SGLang asserts tp_size % dp_size == 0. Implement it as four containers (or four detached processes in one container) pinned with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 / 2,3 / 4,5 / 6,7 on ports 30001-30004, each with --tp 2 --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --trust-remote-code --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 --enable-metrics and the EAGLE 3/1/4 flags, then front them with the SGLang router (python3 -m sglang_router.launch_router --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:30001 ... --port 30000) so the benchmark command's endpoint stays unchanged.

Before spending time on c5, check what the installed image actually supports by running one short SSM command: docker run --rm --entrypoint python3 lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12.post1-cu130 -c 'import importlib;print(bool(importlib.util.find_spec("sglang_router")))' and also inspect python3 -m sglang.launch_server --help for the disaggregation flags. If sglang_router is absent from the image and installing it would need a pip install inside the container, decide in one step: a single pip install attempt is acceptable, an open-ended dependency hunt is not. If the router path is unavailable, fall back to benchmarking ONE of the four tp=2 engines directly on its own port and label the result honestly as 'single tp=2 engine, no router' in matrix-status.json and the report.

Timebox c5 to 45 minutes of wall clock from first launch attempt. If it is not serving benchmarks by then, mark it failed (or partially completed if the single-engine fallback produced numbers), record exactly what was tried and what the error was, and stop. Record the elapsed time in matrix-status.json.

Note in matrix-status.json and later in the report the interpretive caveat for c5: at --max-concurrency 1 a data-parallel router sends every request to a single worker, so c5's TPOT is really a tp=2 single-engine measurement and its value is the TTFT/topology comparison, not throughput scaling.

For every config in this feature, upload artifacts (including server logs of failed launches) to s3://tpot-bench-results-077090643075-us-west-2/runs/b300-matrix-20260809/<config>/ immediately and pull them into results/b300-matrix-20260809/<config>/.

Add stub-based test cases in tests/run-tests.sh for the new config names: --dry-run --config c4-tp8-eagle-triton logs a docker run containing --moe-runner-backend triton and NOT --moe-a2a-backend megamoe; --dry-run --config c5-4x-tp2-router logs four launches with distinct CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES pairs and ports 30001-30004 plus a router on 30000, and contains no --dp flag anywhere.
Commit to harden-ec2-bench-runner. Do not push.
acceptance_criteria: matrix-status.json has a terminal status (completed or failed, with a concrete failure_reason quoting the real error) for both c4-tp8-eagle-triton and c5-4x-tp2-router
Any server log from a failed launch is preserved in S3 and in results/b300-matrix-20260809/<config>/
The c5 implementation uses four independent tp=2 processes and contains no --dp / --enable-dp-attention flag anywhere
c5 elapsed time is recorded and did not exceed the 45-minute timebox
tests/run-tests.sh passes, including new c4/c5 dry-run cases, with at least 22 cases and at least 220 assertions
verification: grep -c 'enable-dp-attention' scripts/b300-run-config.sh returns 0 for the c5 launch path (a commented explanation of why it is absent is fine)
aws s3 ls s3://tpot-bench-results-077090643075-us-west-2/runs/b300-matrix-20260809/ --recursive --region us-west-2 lists c4 and c5 artifacts
